newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INSURERS SEE 12 PCT PREMIUM GROWTH IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INSURERS SEE 12 PCT PREMIUM GROWTH IN 1996.

text.p: Finnish insurers' premium income will grow 12 percent this year to 46 billion markka in total, the Federation of Finnish Insurance Companies said in a statement on Friday.
In individual life and pension insurance -- the fastest growth areas -- premium income will rise 38 percent to almost 10 billion markka, it said.
"Non-life insurance will continue its slight increase and gross premium income is estimated to rise (two percent) to almost 11 billion markka," the federation said.
It expected a decrease in only three areas -- air and sea transports, credit insurance and domestic reinsurance.
Insurers' results would improve compared to last year due to higher investment income, it said, but it gave no estimate.

Bonds have further increased their share of insurers' investment portfolios this year to 36.4 percent of total 217.9 billion markka of investment at end September, i.e to 66 billion markka, it said. At end September 1995, bonds' share of investments -- then 182.4 billion -- was 30.4 percent.
Pension funds' client lending, real estate and other lending have decreased but equity investment at end-September has grown to 14.3 percent from 10.5 percent of total investments, it said.
